attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Faithful: tech stocks falling sharply on Nov 16, after a rout the previous week.

contract.note: Reading 'rout' as a selloff episode, not a losing week, is a fair ordinary reading. A full-week reading would fail, since benchmarks ended the week up.

evidence.note: AP via syndication, Nov 16: Nasdaq down 1.7% midday; Broadcom, AMD and CoreWeave also down. Shows breadth beyond Nvidia.
Kiplinger, Nov 13: broad Friday tech slump, AMD -8.8%, Broadcom -4.8%, Cisco -6.2%.
Major benchmarks still posted weekly gains. This limits how far the week was a rout but doesn't contradict an in-week selloff.

reviews.rationale: Dated reports show substantial, broad tech selling on Nov 16 and a broad tech selloff on Nov 13. That meets the plain-reading support condition. The weekly gains in e3 count against a full-week-rout reading, which the contract fairly does not require.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: Faithful paraphrase: most Nvidia chip buyers were not profiting from the chips.

contract.note: The Q3 2026 window and counting by company are the evaluator's choices. Counting by spending, where hyperscalers dominate, could reverse the result. Marcus supplied no basis.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's own disclosure of a Q3 net loss. One company's company-wide loss cannot show what most buyers earned from the chips.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no representative set of Nvidia buyers and no chip-level profitability measure. The single CoreWeave result cannot settle a claim about most buyers.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Firm 'won't be easy' is a scored forecast. The valuation judgment in the same sentence is rightly left out of this claim.

contract.note: Defining difficulty as weak demand, price concessions or delay is a fair ordinary reading of 'won't be easy'.

evidence.note: Reuters, Nov 5–6: heavy AI-stock selloff. This is evidence for the condition, not for the outcome.
Preliminary orders about six times the offer. This weighs against difficulty, but pricing on Nov 18 and the Nov 19 listing are still in the future.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is Nov 19, after the Nov 16 evaluation date. No completed pricing, withdrawal or postponement is in evidence, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Preliminary orders cannot settle the forecast.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence, following a quote from Dave Troy that he endorses.

semantics.note: Linking 'that collapse' to Nvidia's financing role is a reasonable reading of the context. The wording is partly figurative.

contract.note: 'Shockwaves' could fairly cover market turmoil. The contract asks for linked destabilisation across businesses, so the result depends on that reading.

evidence.note: Reports an undated cut in a guarantee; startup concerns are framed as conditional. No linked disruption across the industry is shown.
JPMAM: neocloud valuations already down, but says it is too soon to tell whether a financing shift will hurt them.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows one undated financing reduction and analysis calling the effects prospective. Nothing establishes material linked disruption across multiple AI businesses during Nov 9–16. Nothing directly refutes it either.
